security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder API keys, documentation links, session IDs, and file handling examples. I confirmed two unsafe eval examples that evaluate agent supplied expressions, and added one semantic finding for the broad Bash allowlist. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a safe expression parser, allowlisted operations, or a dedicated calculator library before publication.
Limit allowed tools to required commands, remove Bash(python *), or require explicit user confirmation for arbitrary Python execution.
Use environment variable examples consistently and state that API keys must never be hardcoded or committed.

content.user_title: Build Python AI Apps with inference.sh
content.value_statement: Python teams need clear SDK guidance for AI apps, agents, streaming, files, and sessions. This skill gives Codex, Claude, and Claude Code practical patterns for inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install and authenticate the inferencesh Python package.
Shows sync and async calls for running inference.sh apps.
Documents streaming progress, task updates, and agent message callbacks.
Covers file uploads, downloads, attachments, and temporary file cleanup.
Guides agent creation with tools, skills, sessions, and human approval.
Provides patterns for batching, retries, concurrency limits, and warm sessions.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include the SDK source code.
Examples require a valid inference.sh API key and account access.
Some examples use placeholder app names that users must replace.
Users must secure tool handlers, webhooks, and file paths in their own code.

use_cases.title: Integrate AI Apps
use_cases.description: Add inference.sh app calls to a Python backend with authentication, inputs, outputs, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Create agents with tools, sub-agents, skills, streaming callbacks, and human approval steps.

use_cases.title: Automate Batch Jobs
use_cases.description: Process many prompts or files with async requests, concurrency limits, retries, and progress tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Python Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the shortest safe Python setup for running one inference.sh app with an environment API key.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add streaming progress updates for a long inference.sh task in a Python command line tool.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh Python agent with one approved client tool, one app tool, and a clear tool result flow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Python integration for async requests, file uploads, retries, sessions, observability, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: Create a first inference.sh Python example for a new backend service.
output_examples.output: A concise setup checklist, authentication guidance, and a minimal app run example described step by step.

output_examples.input: Explain how to process 100 prompts without overloading the service.
output_examples.output: An async batching plan with a concurrency limit, retry strategy, progress reporting, and failure collection.

output_examples.input: Help me build an agent that sends approved notifications.
output_examples.output: A tool design with approval points, safe argument handling, webhook configuration, and result submission guidance.

best_practices: Store API keys in environment variables or managed secrets, not source files.
Require human approval for tools that send messages, write files, or call webhooks.
Use concurrency limits, timeouts, and retries for long async or streaming workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not evaluate agent supplied strings as Python code.
Do not make uploaded files public unless the workflow requires public access.
Do not keep sessions alive longer than the workload needs.

faq.question: What package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the inferencesh Python package for calling inference.sh apps and agents.

faq.question: Does it support async Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async clients, batching, streaming, timeouts, and concurrency control patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with file uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents automatic uploads, manual uploads, file attachments, downloads, and temporary files.

faq.question: Can it build AI agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers template agents, custom agents, tool builders, sub-agents, skills, and approvals.

faq.question: Does it include the SDK implementation?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides usage guidance and examples, not the package source code.

faq.question: What should users secure first?
faq.answer: Secure API keys, webhook secrets, file paths, tool handlers, and any code execution features.
